title: Credit Risk Model Validation & Review-Capacity Lab
summary: A retrospective validation workstation over 30,000 licensed academic credit records, built to compare a non-demographic model with simple references, quantify fixed review workloads, and inspect score-ranked sensitivity without making a lending decision.
outcome: The selected model clears prevalence/random, repayment-delay, and logistic references on repeated paired development evidence, but ties calibrated Extra Trees because the PR-AUC advantage does not clear the prespecified practical margin. At 10% holdout capacity, 600 historical rows contain 431 observed defaults with 71.8% precision and 3.25× lift, each reported with uncertainty.

deployment.provider: Cloudflare Pages and Workers with Neon Postgres
deployment.runtime: Static React application plus read-only Pages Functions; immutable aggregate evidence in Neon Free

metrics: Frozen-holdout PR-AUC 0.5764, AUROC 0.7916, Brier score 0.1314, and 10-bin ECE 0.0124 across 6,000 untouched audit rows
Mean development PR-AUC 0.5513 across six paired folds, against 0.2212 prevalence/random, 0.4480 repayment-delay, 0.5006 logistic, and 0.5452 Extra Trees
Selected-model PR-AUC delta over Extra Trees 0.0061 with paired 95% interval 0.0019–0.0109: reported as a tie against the 0.010 practical margin
At 10% review capacity, 600 rows include 431 historical defaults with precision 0.7183, recall 0.3248, and lift 3.2479, all with 95% intervals
Calibration slope 1.0743 and intercept 0.0757, with a governed sparse-bin warning at n=18
Repayment-status ablation has the largest mean PR-AUC loss, 0.0982 with 95% interval 0.0845–0.1141
stages: Validate the integrity-pinned UCI workbook and exclude demographic fields from model inputs
Lock selection on train and validation data while freezing the 6,000-row holdout under a private integrity record
Run paired repeated stratified development evaluation against three simple references and Extra Trees
Measure holdout ranking, calibration, five review workloads, non-demographic cohort robustness, and feature-group reliance
Build and validate versioned aggregate and 30,000-row non-demographic analyst artifacts
Serve the read-only validation workstation with immutable release health and fail-closed availability
architecture: Local Python pipeline validates the licensed workbook, reproduces model evidence, and records source, split, command, tool, and revision lineage
A version-4 static analyst artifact contains approved non-demographic fields, derived measures, retrospective out-of-fold scores, and deterministic ranks for all 30,000 rows
The React workstation computes cohort views client-side and renders model evidence from the immutable evaluation envelope using semantic HTML and native SVG
Cloudflare Pages serves the application and artifact; read-only Pages Functions expose health and current-release evidence
Neon stores one immutable aggregate release behind a least-privilege runtime credential; viewers have no write path
evaluation: Fixed stratified 60/20/20 split with random state 20260801; model selection is locked before the frozen holdout audit
Two repeats of three shared stratified folds over 24,000 development rows produce paired deltas and 95% intervals
Practical margins decide whether superiority is resolved; otherwise the comparison is a tie
Every approved 5%, 10%, 20%, 35%, and 50% workload reports queue composition, precision, recall, lift, incremental yield, and uncertainty
Calibration slope/intercept, sparse-bin warnings, sample-size-aware non-demographic cohorts, and feature-group ablations qualify the headline result
Evaluation schema version 2 binds UTC generation time, source integrity, evaluated revision, split identities, command, and tool versions
operationalTradeoffs: The source has one target horizon, so the fixed stratified holdout is not calendar-time or out-of-time validation.
Repeated folds reduce dependence on one development split but remain correlated views of the same historical academic population.
Capacity intervals describe one audit sample; they are not staffing, loss, revenue, or benefit forecasts.
Feature-group ablations show fitted-model reliance and must not be used as causes, consumer explanations, or adverse-action reasons.
Sex, education, marriage, and age remain local and aggregate-only for fairness review; they are excluded from model inputs and public individual records.
The approximately 15 MB governed analyst artifact dominates first-load transfer in exchange for full-record, client-side analysis without a per-record API.
The free-tier deployment has no scheduled monitoring or uptime guarantee; required release and artifact failures are handled with an explicit unavailable state.
disclaimer: This is a public, retrospective academic research demonstration using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset under CC BY 4.0. It is not validated for lending use and does not make an approval, denial, eligibility, pricing, adverse-action, or lending recommendation.

story.recruiterSummary: A model-risk reviewer can compare a non-demographic credit model with simple references, see where evidence is unresolved, test five historical review workloads with uncertainty, and inspect the exact rows behind the simulation without receiving a lending recommendation.
story.technicalNarrative: The central control is separation: model selection stays on train and validation data, the 6,000-row holdout is frozen under a private integrity record, and repeated stability tests run only on the 24,000 development rows. All candidates share the same folds, and a practical-margin rule turns small unresolved differences into ties. A versioned evaluation envelope then carries split identities, uncertainty, calibration warnings, cohort sample sizes, ablations, revision, command, and tool lineage into a 30,000-row non-demographic analyst artifact. The React workstation keeps holdout, development, artifact, and live-health evidence visually distinct, while Cloudflare and Neon provide a zero-dollar read-only serving path.
scalabilityRoadmap: The 15 MB static analyst artifact is the current load constraint. At materially larger row counts, move filtered aggregates and paginated records behind a read-only API while retaining the same public schema and privacy tests.

The evaluation is offline and batch by design. A recurring validation program would need new time-indexed data, scheduled runs, drift ownership, alert thresholds, and evidence retention before any service automation.
Neon stores one immutable aggregate release. Multiple concurrent releases would require an explicit release catalog and retention policy rather than overwriting the current snapshot.
No operational credit workflow should be added until external, out-of-time, prospective, legal, and fair-lending validation supports that change in scope.
story.executiveSummary: The selected model is useful for retrospective research but not uniquely superior to every credible alternative. Its frozen-holdout PR-AUC is 0.5764, and repeated paired evidence clears prevalence/random, repayment-delay, and logistic references. Against calibrated Extra Trees the PR-AUC gain is 0.0061 with a 95% interval of 0.0019–0.0109, so it does not clear the 0.010 margin and is reported as a tie. At 10% historical review capacity, 600 rows include 431 observed defaults with 71.8% precision and 3.25× lift. The product shows that workload and its uncertainty without treating rank sensitivity as an approval, denial, price, or consumer reason.
story.intendedUser: A credit-risk analyst or model-risk reviewer assessing retrospective model readiness and review-capacity evidence.

limitations: One historical academic population with one target horizon; no calendar-time or true out-of-time validation.
No external, geographic, prospective, drift, operational, causal, loss, pricing, or lending-decision validation.
Repeated folds remain correlated views of the same development population.
Capacity intervals describe the frozen audit sample, not staffing needs or financial benefit.
Cross-cohort PR-AUC values reflect different prevalence levels and are not directly comparable without context.
Ablations are model-reliance evidence only and cannot be used as consumer explanations or adverse-action reasons.
The free-tier public demonstration has no uptime guarantee or scheduled monitoring.
Automated accessibility checks do not replace manual keyboard, zoom, screen-reader, and contrast review.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a 30,000-record credit-risk validation lab that kept a 6,000-row holdout frozen, compared the selected model with random, rule-based, logistic, and Extra Trees references across six paired development folds, and reported a tie when the practical margin was not met.

Designed a five-point review-capacity simulation with confidence intervals; at 10% capacity, the historical queue contained 431 observed defaults among 600 rows with 71.8% precision, 32.5% recall, and 3.25× lift, explicitly bounded as research evidence rather than a lending decision.

Shipped a privacy-preserving React, Cloudflare, and Neon research workstation with 30,000 full records, no demographic fields in public individual views, immutable release lineage, fail-closed availability, and a clean gate covering 27 Python and 16 web tests.

Added calibration slope/intercept, sparse-bin warnings, sample-size-aware non-demographic cohort checks, and feature-group ablations, framing the outputs as stability and model-reliance evidence rather than causal or adverse-action explanations.
